contracts.classification: direct pinned-source observation plus absence-of-contract limit
facts: ID0 media body contains an 8-byte timestamp then raw media; ID1 carries raw media without a timestamp. Neither is a protobuf frame.

Old OpenAuto writes bodies as a byte stream or recuts them by OMX input capacity. A single media indication, a transport fragment, a NAL and an access unit are distinct boundaries. No equality contract is established by this pin.
ACK value1 is issued after invoking output write for each delivered indication. It does not certify codec output or physical display.
recommended_local_policy: Strip message ID and timestamp before video parser. Own copied compressed bytes before an upstream indication ACK if processing continues asynchronously. Do not ACK each NAL or frame.

Use a bounded Annex-B assembler before a complete-AU decoder wrapper; retain media timestamp separately and state AU timestamp association rules explicitly. No phone timestamp unit guarantee is derived from this pin.

facts: OpenH264 decoder example includes start-code prefix. WelsDecodeBs searches a start prefix, copies/unescapes caller data into internal raw storage, and parses the final NAL at the end of each input call. It is not evidence of acceptance of arbitrary split NAL/start-code input.

Synchronous NoDelay runs DecodeFrame2(data), then DecodeFrame2(NULL,0) using the same output info. A body containing multiple AUs can produce results that this single-output wrapper does not preserve.
recommended_local_policy: Complete-AU-only codec provider is an explicit local restriction; do not present it as all Android Auto framing compatibility. Reject or assemble partial NALs, retain state across input chunk boundaries, and reject over-limit or ambiguous AUs.

For threads0 synchronous calls, keep source immutable until return; copy ready output before another decode/flush/reset/uninitialize. This lifetime policy is stricter than relying on codec buffer reuse details.

facts: Output is available only when iBufferStatus==1. I420 planes are codec picture pointers, not caller storage; dimensions are visible cropped dimensions. Y uses iStride[0], both U and V use iStride[1].
Normal output already adds crop offsets to returned pointers. Do not crop a second time. Reordering stores and returns SBufferInfo with the originating picture timestamp.
Return0 without iBufferStatus1 does not establish a frame; nonzero decoding state can accompany concealment output.
recommended_local_policy: Disable error concealment for a fail-closed host proof, independently require ready/format/dimensions/nonnull pointers and valid strides, then copy each row to bounded tight owned YUV420.
A sink PAUSED must retain copied output and retry delivery without re-decoding the AU. Preserve returned output timestamp, not the most recent input timestamp, for reordered output.

contracts.classification: direct pinned-source observation; not stream compatibility test
facts: RELEASES v2.0.0 explicitly records Main/High B-frame decoding; v2.2.0 and v2.3.0 record B-frame fixes. The README Baseline feature list is not a reliable exclusive capability statement.

Actual SPS parser accepts Baseline/Main/High as well as selected other profiles. It rejects chroma_format_idc>1, bit depths other than8, and interlaced frame_mbs_only_flag0. Supporting Main/High does not establish every syntax feature or phone stream compatibility.
With threads0, non-Baseline/non-scalable-Baseline pictures still pass through reordering state. No-B-slice streams can retain a final picture.
recommended_local_policy: Validate SPS/profile/chroma/bitdepth/progressive/coded and visible sizes and refs before forwarding parameter sets to upstream. A narrower wrapper policy must be recorded distinctly from upstream capability.
Include actual Main/High/B-frame host fixtures, output order and timestamp assertions, and EOS flush validation when the wrapper claims these formats.

contracts.classification: direct pinned-source observation plus recommended lifecycle policy
facts: DECODER_OPTION_END_OF_STREAM sets context EOS. FlushFrame releases reordered buffered pictures only if EOS and remaining count>0; it returns0 even when no output is produced and does not universally clear caller buffer info.
GetOption(NUM_OF_FRAMES_REMAINING_IN_BUFFER) reads reorder count. API documents FlushFrame for profile_idc!=66. This does not reconstruct an unfinished compressed AU by itself.

Uninitialize frees decoder context/picture storage; create/destroy and initialize are separate APIs. SetOption threads0 is applied before Initialize to avoid changing live decoder context-count storage.
recommended_local_policy: Finish/validate the owned Annex-B/AU assembler before EOS. On flush, clear pointers and buffer info per iteration, use bounded remaining-count checks, and copy output before the next call.

Stop/session reset drops pending source bytes and pending copied output and reconstructs codec instance so no stale SPS/reference picture crosses sessions. Flush-drain is distinct from discard-on-stop.

contracts.classification: direct source constants and allocation formula; not peak heap measurement
facts: InitBsBuffer allocates MIN_ACCESS_UNIT_CAPACITY1048576 * MAX_BUFFERED_NUM3 = 3145728 bytes raw bitstream storage. Large input can expand it; there are additional context/array allocations.

Single-thread picture list size is SPS max_num_ref_frames+2. Each picture allocates align32(codedWidth+64)*align32(codedHeight+64)*3/2 pixel bytes and per-macroblock correctness, type, motion vectors and reference indices. Cropped visible dimensions alone do not bound coded allocations.

Public SetOption has no general total-heap-cap allocator control. Wrapper SPS/NAL/AU/output caps constrain inputs and growth but do not establish an enforced total heap limit or no-allocation property.
recommended_local_policy: Bound coded macroblock dimensions as well as visible cropped dimensions and references before OpenH264 receives SPS. Record wrapper working-storage limits separately from upstream dynamic heap.
For future native port, provide bounded allocator integration or instrument actual heap usage/failure paths; do not infer Garmin RAM availability from source formulas.

contracts.classification: static portability gap; no ARM compile or execution
facts: ARM NEON defines in arch.mk are gated by USE_ASM=Yes; C/C++ fallback CPU feature detector returns0 without the architecture acceleration macros.

This is still C++ hosted code: new/delete, aligned malloc/free, gettimeofday, CPU-count discovery and non-Windows pthread/semaphore interfaces remain. threads0 selects synchronous decoding but does not remove source/link platform requirements.
Linux aarch64 host execution would prove neither ARMv6 code generation, Garmin ABI, on-device runtime, real-time decoding, hardware acceleration nor display output.
recommended_local_policy: Future native design needs ARMv6 soft-float C++ runtime/allocator/memory/time/platform shim, serialized ownership and measured decoding plus conversion cost. This review does not supply or run such a shim.

unproven: Any actual Pixel Android Auto compressed stream or current projection negotiation
No-AUD and parameter-set/session timestamp association beyond the own assembler policy
GarminOS freestanding C++ runtime or total-heap cap
Original Garmin loading/UI/touch/USB-host or firmware acceptance
Hardware H264 acceleration API and on-device display
